reductions.name: Provability over RCA₀*
reductions.description: Implication provable over RCA₀*, i.e. RCA₀ with Σ⁰₁-induction replaced by Δ⁰₀-induction and the totality of exponentiation (Simpson–Smith 1986).

reductions.name: Provability over RCA₀
reductions.description: Implication provable over the base system RCA₀.

reductions.name: ω-model implication
reductions.phrase: every ω-model of {a} is a model of {b}
reductions.description: Every ω-model (equivalently every Turing ideal) satisfying the first statement satisfies the second.

reductions.name: Strong Weihrauch reduction
reductions.description: There are Turing functionals Φ, Ψ such that for every instance X of the second problem, Φ(X) is an instance of the first, and for every solution Y of Φ(X), Ψ(Y) is a solution of X (Ψ has no access to X).

reductions.name: Weihrauch reduction
reductions.description: Uniform reduction: Φ maps instances to instances, Ψ maps (original instance, solution) to solutions.

reductions.name: Strong computable reduction
reductions.description: Every instance X of the second problem computes an instance X̂ of the first such that every solution of X̂ computes a solution of X.

reductions.name: Computable reduction
reductions.description: Every instance X of the second problem computes an instance X̂ of the first such that for every solution Ŷ of X̂, X ⊕ Ŷ computes a solution of X.

reductions.name: Generalized Weihrauch reduction
reductions.description: Uniform reduction allowing finitely many adaptive uses of the first problem (Hirschfeldt–Jockusch 2016).

properties.name: Cone avoidance
properties.description: For every set Z and every C ≰_T Z, every Z-computable instance has a solution Y such that C ≰_T Z ⊕ Y.

properties.name: PA avoidance
properties.description: For every set Z which is not of PA degree, every Z-computable instance has a solution Y such that Z ⊕ Y is not of PA degree.

properties.name: Low basis
properties.description: For every Z, every Z-computable instance has a solution Y such that (Z ⊕ Y)' ≤_T Z'.

properties.name: Computably true
properties.description: Every instance X has a solution computable in X.

properties.name: Π¹₁-conservative over RCA₀
properties.description: RCA₀ + the statement proves no Π¹₁ sentence which is not already provable in RCA₀.

properties.name: Preservation of hyperimmunity
properties.description: For every set Z and every Z-hyperimmune set A, every Z-computable instance has a solution Y such that A is (Z ⊕ Y)-hyperimmune.

properties.name: Preservation of Δ⁰₂ definitions
properties.description: For every Z and every set A which is not Δ⁰₂(Z), every Z-computable instance has a solution Y such that A is not Δ⁰₂(Z ⊕ Y) (Wang).

properties.name: Preservation of the arithmetic hierarchy
properties.description: For every Z, every n, and every set A which is not Σ⁰ₙ(Z) (resp. Π⁰ₙ, Δ⁰ₙ), every Z-computable instance has a solution Y such that A is still not Σ⁰ₙ(Z ⊕ Y) (resp. Π⁰ₙ, Δ⁰ₙ).

properties.name: Preservation of c.b.-immunity
properties.description: For every Z and every set A which is computably bounded immune relative to Z, every Z-computable instance has a solution Y such that A is c.b.-immune relative to Z ⊕ Y (Patey, "Partial orders and immunity").

properties.name: Preservation of dependent hyperimmunity
properties.description: Preservation of dependent hyperimmunity, in the sense of Patey, "Partial orders and immunity in reverse mathematics".

properties.name: Preservation of 2-hyperimmunity
properties.description: Preservation of 2-hyperimmunity in the sense of Liu and Patey, "The reverse mathematics of the thin set and Erdős–Moser theorems": for every set C and every C-2-hyperimmune pair, every C-computable instance has a solution G relative to which the pair is still 2-hyperimmune.

statements.label: \mathsf{CL}_{\mathrm{c}}
statements.name: Cousin's lemma for continuous gauges
statements.definition: For every continuous gauge $\delta : [0,1] \to \mathbb{R}^+$ there is a $\delta$-fine tagged partition of $[0,1]$.

statements.label: \mathsf{CL}_{\mathrm{B1}}
statements.name: Cousin's lemma for Baire class 1 gauges
statements.definition: Cousin's lemma restricted to gauges of Baire class 1.

statements.label: \mathsf{UKT}
statements.name: Uniform Kruskal theorem
statements.definition: The uniform Kruskal theorem of Freund, Rathjen and Weiermann: a uniform version of Kruskal's theorem for recursive data types given by normal transformations of well partial orders.

statements.label: \mathsf{TLPP}
statements.name: Transfinite leftmost path principle
statements.definition: Towsner's transfinite leftmost path principle; see the source.

statements.label: \mathsf{JD}
statements.name: Jordan decomposition theorem
statements.definition: Every function $f : [0,1] \to \mathbb{R}$ of bounded variation is the difference of two non-decreasing functions.

statements.label: \mathsf{JD}_{\mathrm{c}}
statements.name: Jordan decomposition theorem (continuous)
statements.definition: Every continuous function of bounded variation on $[0,1]$ is the difference of two continuous non-decreasing functions.

statements.label: \mathsf{BV}\text{-}\mathsf{DIFF}
statements.name: Differentiability of BV functions
statements.definition: Every function of bounded variation on $[0,1]$ is differentiable almost everywhere.

statements.label: \mathsf{ART}^2_2
statements.name: Ramsey theorem for additive colourings
statements.definition: Ramsey's theorem for pairs restricted to additive colourings (colourings into a finite semigroup with $c(i,k) = c(i,j) \cdot c(j,k)$), asserting an infinite homogeneous set.
statements.instance: A coloring $c : [\mathbb{N}]^2 \to S$ into a finite semigroup with $c(i,k) = c(i,j) \cdot c(j,k)$.
statements.solution: An infinite homogeneous set.

statements.label: \mathsf{BC}
statements.name: Büchi's complementation theorem
statements.definition: Every language recognized by a nondeterministic Büchi automaton has a complement recognized by a nondeterministic Büchi automaton.

statements.label: \mathsf{FPT}
statements.name: Fishburn's possibility theorem
statements.definition: Fishburn's possibility theorem for countable societies: there is a social welfare function satisfying Arrow's conditions.

statements.label: \mathsf{AHT}
statements.name: Adjacent Hindman's theorem
statements.definition: Hindman's theorem where homogeneity is only required for finite sums of adjacent elements.
statements.solution: An infinite set whose finite sums of adjacent elements are monochromatic.

statements.label: \mathsf{HIL}
statements.name: Hilbert's theorem
statements.definition: Variant of Hindman's theorem studied by Hirst, equivalent to the infinite pigeonhole principle; see the source.

statements.label: \mathsf{FIN}_k
statements.name: Gowers' FIN_k theorem
statements.definition: Gowers' pigeonhole principle for $\mathrm{FIN}_k$, a generalization of Hindman's theorem.
statements.instance: A number $k$ and a finite coloring of $\mathrm{FIN}_k$.
statements.solution: An infinite block sequence whose generated combinatorial subspace is monochromatic.

statements.label: \mathsf{AP}
statements.name: Existence of almost periodic points
statements.definition: Every continuous map on a compact metric space has an almost periodic point.

statements.label: \mathsf{ACA}^+
statements.name: ω-th jump
statements.definition: For every $X$, the $\omega$-th jump $X^{(\omega)}$ exists.
statements.solution: The $\omega$-th jump $X^{(\omega)}$.

statements.label: \mathsf{ACA}'
statements.name: Finite jumps
statements.definition: For every $n$ and every $X$, the $n$-th jump $X^{(n)}$ exists.
statements.solution: The $n$-th jump $X^{(n)}$.

statements.label: \mathsf{WOP}(\varepsilon_X)
statements.name: Well-ordering principle for ε
statements.definition: If $X$ is a well-ordering, then so is $\varepsilon_X$.

statements.label: \mathsf{BRD}_{\mathbb{H}}
statements.name: Finite big Ramsey degrees of Henson graphs
statements.definition: The Henson graphs have finite big Ramsey degrees.

statements.label: \mathsf{CPT}\Rightarrow\mathsf{LEB}
statements.name: Compact spaces are Lebesgue
statements.definition: Every compact metric space is Lebesgue: every open covering has a Lebesgue number.

statements.label: \mathsf{BROOKS}
statements.name: Brooks' theorem
statements.definition: Brooks' theorem for arbitrary countable graphs: a connected graph of maximum degree $d \ge 3$ other than $K_{d+1}$ is $d$-colorable.

statements.label: \mathbf{3}\text{-}\mathsf{BQO}
statements.name: The antichain with three elements is bqo
statements.definition: The discrete order with three elements is a better quasi-order.

statements.label: \mathsf{INV}
statements.name: Brouwer invariance theorems
statements.definition: Brouwer's invariance of dimension and domain theorems (in the formulations of Kihara 2020).

statements.label: \mathsf{EVP}
statements.name: Ekeland's variational principle
statements.definition: Ekeland's variational principle for lower semicontinuous functions on complete separable metric spaces.

statements.label: \mathsf{SCT}
statements.name: Size-change termination criterion
statements.definition: The size-change termination criterion of Lee, Jones and Ben-Amram.

statements.label: \mathsf{TET}
statements.name: Tietze extension theorem
statements.definition: Versions of the Tietze extension theorem for functions with moduli of uniform continuity.

statements.label: \mathsf{HST}
statements.name: Helly's selection theorem
statements.definition: Every bounded sequence of functions of bounded variation has a subsequence converging in the weak* topology.

statements.label: \mathsf{TT}
statements.name: Tree theorem for all exponents
statements.definition: For every $n$ and $k$, the tree theorem $\mathsf{TT}^n_k$ holds.
statements.instance: Numbers $n, k$ and a coloring of the $n$-element chains of $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$ with $k$ colors.
statements.solution: A homogeneous subtree isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$.

statements.label: \mathsf{PR}^2
statements.name: Packed Ramsey theorem for pairs
statements.definition: Erdős–Galvin packed Ramsey theorem for pairs: every coloring admits an infinite "packed" set using few colors; see the source.

statements.label: \mathsf{HB}
statements.name: Hahn–Banach theorem (separable)
statements.definition: Every bounded linear functional on a closed subspace of a separable Banach space extends to the whole space with the same norm.
statements.instance: A separable Banach space, a closed subspace and a bounded functional on it.
statements.solution: A norm-preserving extension of the functional.

statements.label: \mathsf{RCA}_0
statements.name: Base system
statements.definition: The base system: no axiom beyond the base theory of the reduction under consideration. Over theories this is RCA₀ (recursive comprehension and $\Sigma^0_1$-induction), or RCA₀* when working over RCA₀*; as a problem it is the identity problem.

statements.label: \mathsf{WKL}
statements.name: Weak König's lemma
statements.definition: Every infinite subtree of $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$ has an infinite path.
statements.solution: An infinite path through $T$.

statements.label: \Sigma^0_1\text{-}\mathsf{SEP}
statements.name: Σ⁰₁ separation
statements.definition: For every pair of disjoint $\Sigma^0_1$ sets $A, B$, there is a set $S$ with $A \subseteq S$ and $S \cap B = \emptyset$.
statements.solution: A set $S$ separating $A$ from $B$.

statements.label: \mathsf{WWKL}
statements.name: Weak weak König's lemma
statements.definition: Every binary tree $T$ of positive measure, i.e. $\lim_s |T \cap 2^s| / 2^s > 0$, has an infinite path.
statements.instance: A binary tree of positive measure.
statements.solution: An infinite path through it.

statements.label: \mathsf{DNR}
statements.name: Diagonally non-recursive functions
statements.definition: For every set $X$, there is a function $f$ such that $f(e) \neq \Phi^X_e(e)$ for every $e$.
statements.solution: A function $f$ which is diagonally non-computable relative to $X$.

statements.label: \mathsf{ACA}
statements.name: Arithmetical comprehension
statements.definition: Every set defined by an arithmetical formula exists. Equivalently over RCA₀, every set has a Turing jump.
statements.solution: The Turing jump $X'$.

statements.label: \mathsf{ATR}
statements.name: Arithmetical transfinite recursion
statements.definition: Arithmetical comprehension can be iterated along any countable well-ordering.

statements.label: \Pi^1_1\text{-}\mathsf{CA}
statements.name: Π¹₁ comprehension
statements.definition: Every set defined by a $\Pi^1_1$ formula exists.

statements.label: \mathsf{I}\Sigma^0_1
statements.name: Σ⁰₁ induction
statements.definition: The induction scheme restricted to $\Sigma^0_1$ formulas.

statements.label: \mathsf{B}\Sigma^0_2
statements.name: Σ⁰₂ collection
statements.definition: For every $\Sigma^0_2$ formula $\varphi$ and every $n$: if $\forall i < n\, \exists y\, \varphi(i, y)$ then there is a bound $b$ with $\forall i < n\, \exists y < b\, \varphi(i, y)$.

statements.label: \mathsf{I}\Delta^0_2
statements.name: Δ⁰₂ induction
statements.definition: The induction scheme restricted to $\Delta^0_2$ formulas.

statements.label: \mathsf{I}\Sigma^0_2
statements.name: Σ⁰₂ induction
statements.definition: The induction scheme restricted to $\Sigma^0_2$ formulas.

statements.label: \mathsf{SRT}^2_3
statements.name: Stable Ramsey's theorem for pairs (3 colors)
statements.definition: Every stable coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^2 \to 3$ has an infinite homogeneous set.
statements.solution: An infinite homogeneous set.

statements.label: \mathsf{ADC}
statements.name: Ascending or descending chain
statements.definition: Every infinite linear order has an infinite ascending chain or an infinite descending chain (as sets, without the order of enumeration).
statements.solution: An infinite set which is an ascending chain or a descending chain.

statements.label: \mathsf{HT}
statements.name: Hindman's theorem
statements.definition: For every finite coloring of $\mathbb{N}$ there is an infinite set $H$ such that all nonempty finite sums of distinct elements of $H$ have the same color.
statements.solution: An infinite set all of whose finite sums have the same color.

statements.label: \mathsf{HT}^{\le 3}_3
statements.name: Hindman's theorem for sums of at most 3 elements (3 colors)
statements.definition: For every coloring $c : \mathbb{N} \to 3$ there is an infinite set $H$ such that all sums of at most 3 distinct elements of $H$ have the same color.
statements.solution: An infinite set as above.

statements.label: \mathsf{HT}^{\le 2}_2
statements.name: Hindman's theorem for sums of at most 2 elements
statements.definition: For every coloring $c : \mathbb{N} \to 2$ there is an infinite set $H$ such that all sums of at most 2 distinct elements of $H$ have the same color.
statements.solution: An infinite set as above.

statements.label: \mathsf{HT}^{=2}_2
statements.name: Hindman's theorem for sums of exactly 2 elements
statements.definition: For every coloring $c : \mathbb{N} \to 2$ there is an infinite set $H$ such that all sums of exactly 2 distinct elements of $H$ have the same color.
statements.solution: An infinite set as above.

statements.label: \mathsf{RSg}
statements.name: Rival–Sands theorem for graphs
statements.definition: Every infinite graph $G$ contains an infinite subset $H$ such that every vertex of $G$ is adjacent to none, exactly one, or infinitely many vertices of $H$.
statements.solution: An infinite set $H$ as above.

statements.label: \mathsf{RSpo}
statements.name: Rival–Sands theorem for partial orders of finite width
statements.definition: Every infinite partial order $P$ of finite width contains an infinite chain $C$ such that every element of $P$ is comparable with no element or with infinitely many elements of $C$.
statements.instance: An infinite partial order of finite width.
statements.solution: An infinite chain $C$ as above.

statements.label: \mathsf{RSpo}_3
statements.name: Rival–Sands theorem for partial orders of width at most 3
statements.definition: The Rival–Sands theorem restricted to partial orders of width at most 3.
statements.instance: An infinite partial order of width at most 3.
statements.solution: An infinite chain $C$ such that every element is comparable with no element or with infinitely many elements of $C$.

statements.label: \mathsf{RSpo}_{\mathrm{CD}}
statements.name: Rival–Sands theorem for unions of two chains
statements.definition: The Rival–Sands theorem restricted to partial orders decomposable into two chains.
statements.instance: An infinite partial order which is a union of two chains.
statements.solution: An infinite chain $C$ such that every element is comparable with no element or with infinitely many elements of $C$.

statements.label: \mathsf{ERT}
statements.name: Eventually constant Ramsey-type principle
statements.definition: Combinatorial principle of Davis, Hirschfeldt, Hirst, Pardo, Pauly and Yokoyama, equivalent to $\mathsf{I}\Sigma^0_1$ over RCA₀*; see the source.

statements.label: \mathsf{ECT}
statements.name: Eventually constant tail principle
statements.definition: For every coloring $c : \mathbb{N} \to k$ there is $n$ such that every color occurring after $n$ occurs infinitely often. Equivalent to $\mathsf{I}\Sigma^0_2$ over RCA₀*.

statements.label: \mathsf{W}2\text{-}\mathsf{RAN}
statements.name: Existence of weakly 2-randoms
statements.definition: For every $Z$ there is a set which is weakly 2-random relative to $Z$.
statements.solution: A set weakly 2-random relative to $Z$.

statements.label: \mathsf{CR}\text{-}\mathsf{RAN}
statements.name: Existence of computable randoms
statements.definition: For every $Z$ there is a set which is computably random relative to $Z$.
statements.solution: A set computably random relative to $Z$.

statements.label: \mathsf{SR}\text{-}\mathsf{RAN}
statements.name: Existence of Schnorr randoms
statements.definition: For every $Z$ there is a set which is Schnorr random relative to $Z$.
statements.solution: A set Schnorr random relative to $Z$.

statements.label: \mathsf{BRT}^2_2
statements.name: Bounded Ramsey's theorem for pairs
statements.definition: For every coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^2 \to 2$ whose 1-homogeneous sets have bounded size, there is an infinite 0-homogeneous set.
statements.instance: A coloring whose 1-homogeneous sets are of bounded size.
statements.solution: An infinite 0-homogeneous set.

statements.label: \mathsf{BRT}^3_2
statements.name: Bounded Ramsey's theorem for triples
statements.definition: For every coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^3 \to 2$ whose 1-homogeneous sets have bounded size, there is an infinite 0-homogeneous set.
statements.instance: A coloring of triples whose 1-homogeneous sets are of bounded size.
statements.solution: An infinite 0-homogeneous set.

statements.label: \mathsf{OVW}
statements.name: Ordered variable word theorem
statements.definition: For every finite alphabet $A$ and finite coloring of the words over $A$, there is a word $c_0$ and an infinite sequence of left-variable words $w_1, w_2, \dots$ such that all words $c_0 \cdot w_1[a_1] \cdots w_k[a_k]$ have the same color.
statements.instance: A finite alphabet $A$ and a finite coloring of $A^{<\mathbb{N}}$.
statements.solution: A word $c_0$ and an infinite sequence of left-variable words as in the statement.

statements.label: \mathsf{fin}\text{-}\mathsf{COH}
statements.name: Finite cohesiveness principle
statements.definition: COH restricted to finite sequences of sets.
statements.instance: A finite sequence of sets $R_0, \dots, R_{n-1}$.
statements.solution: An infinite set $C$ with $C \subseteq^* R_i$ or $C \subseteq^* \overline{R_i}$ for each $i < n$.

statements.label: \mathsf{CAC}
statements.name: Chain–antichain principle
statements.definition: Every infinite partial order has an infinite chain or an infinite antichain.
statements.solution: An infinite chain or an infinite antichain.

statements.label: \mathsf{SCAC}
statements.name: Stable chain–antichain principle
statements.definition: Every infinite stable partial order has an infinite chain or an infinite antichain.
statements.solution: An infinite chain or an infinite antichain.

statements.label: \mathsf{ADS}
statements.name: Ascending or descending sequence
statements.definition: Every infinite linear order has an infinite ascending or an infinite descending sequence.
statements.solution: An infinite ascending or descending sequence.

statements.label: \mathsf{SADS}
statements.name: Stable ascending or descending sequence
statements.definition: Every infinite linear order of type $\omega + \omega^*$ has an infinite ascending or descending sequence.
statements.instance: An infinite linear order of type $\omega + \omega^*$.
statements.solution: An infinite ascending or descending sequence.

statements.label: \mathsf{CADS}
statements.name: Cohesive ascending or descending sequence
statements.definition: Every infinite linear order has a stable suborder, i.e. an infinite suborder of type $\omega$, $\omega^*$ or $\omega + \omega^*$.
statements.solution: An infinite stable suborder.

statements.label: \mathsf{RT}^1_2
statements.name: Infinite pigeonhole principle (2 colors)
statements.definition: Every coloring $f : \mathbb{N} \to 2$ has an infinite homogeneous set.
statements.solution: An infinite set $H$ on which $f$ is constant.

statements.label: \mathsf{RT}^1_3
statements.name: Infinite pigeonhole principle (3 colors)
statements.definition: Every coloring $f : \mathbb{N} \to 3$ has an infinite homogeneous set.
statements.solution: An infinite set $H$ on which $f$ is constant.

statements.label: \mathsf{RT}^1_{<\infty}
statements.name: Infinite pigeonhole principle (finitely many colors)
statements.definition: For every $k$, every coloring $f : \mathbb{N} \to k$ has an infinite homogeneous set.
statements.instance: A number $k$ and a coloring $f : \mathbb{N} \to k$.
statements.solution: An infinite set $H$ on which $f$ is constant.

statements.label: \mathsf{RT}^2_2
statements.name: Ramsey's theorem for pairs
statements.definition: Every coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^2 \to 2$ has an infinite homogeneous set.
statements.solution: An infinite set $H$ such that $f$ is constant on $[H]^2$.

statements.label: \mathsf{RT}^2_3
statements.name: Ramsey's theorem for pairs (3 colors)
statements.definition: Every coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^2 \to 3$ has an infinite homogeneous set.
statements.solution: An infinite set $H$ such that $f$ is constant on $[H]^2$.

statements.label: \mathsf{RT}^3_2
statements.name: Ramsey's theorem for triples
statements.definition: Every coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^3 \to 2$ has an infinite homogeneous set.
statements.solution: An infinite set $H$ such that $f$ is constant on $[H]^3$.

statements.label: \mathsf{SRT}^2_2
statements.name: Stable Ramsey's theorem for pairs
statements.definition: Every stable coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^2 \to 2$ (i.e. $\lim_y f(x, y)$ exists for every $x$) has an infinite homogeneous set.
statements.solution: An infinite set $H$ such that $f$ is constant on $[H]^2$.

statements.label: \mathsf{D}^2_2
statements.name: Δ⁰₂ subset principle
statements.definition: For every stable coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^2 \to 2$ there is an infinite set $H$ and a color $i$ such that $\lim_y f(x, y) = i$ for all $x \in H$. Equivalently, every $\Delta^0_2$ set has an infinite subset in it or its complement.
statements.solution: An infinite set which is limit-homogeneous for $f$.

statements.label: \mathsf{COH}
statements.name: Cohesiveness principle
statements.definition: For every sequence of sets $R_0, R_1, \dots$, there is an infinite set $C$ such that for every $i$, either $C \subseteq^* R_i$ or $C \subseteq^* \overline{R_i}$.
statements.solution: An infinite $\vec R$-cohesive set.

statements.label: \mathsf{EM}
statements.name: Erdős–Moser theorem
statements.definition: Every infinite tournament has an infinite transitive subtournament.
statements.solution: An infinite set $H$ on which $T$ is transitive.

statements.name: Ascending or descending sequence + Erdős–Moser theorem

statements.solution: An atomic model of $T$.

statements.name: Almost stable Ramsey for measure

statements.solution: An infinite increasing-homogeneous sequence of sets.

statements.label: \mathsf{SIPTT}^{2}_{<\infty}
statements.name: Stable increasing polarized tree theorem for pairs (finitely many colors)
statements.definition: Polarized version of the tree theorem $\mathsf{TT}^{2}_{k}$: one asks for a sequence of subtrees isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$, one per coordinate, and only increasing chains are considered; restricted to stable colorings.
statements.instance: A coloring of the 2-element chains of $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$.
statements.solution: A sequence of 2 subtrees isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$ which is homogeneous in the polarized sense.

statements.label: \mathsf{SIPTT}^{2}_2
statements.name: Stable increasing polarized tree theorem for pairs (2 colors)
statements.definition: Polarized version of the tree theorem $\mathsf{TT}^{2}_{2}$: one asks for a sequence of subtrees isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$, one per coordinate, and only increasing chains are considered; restricted to stable colorings.
statements.instance: A coloring of the 2-element chains of $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$.
statements.solution: A sequence of 2 subtrees isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$ which is homogeneous in the polarized sense.

statements.label: \mathsf{SPT}^{2}_{<\infty}
statements.name: Stable polarized Ramsey theorem for pairs (finitely many colors)
statements.definition: For every stable coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{2} \to k$ for every $k$, there are infinite sets $H_1, \dots, H_{2}$ such that $f$ is constant on all sets $\{x_1, \dots, x_{2}\} \in [\mathbb{N}]^{2}$ with $x_i \in H_i$.
statements.solution: An infinite homogeneous sequence of sets $(H_1, \dots, H_n)$.

statements.label: \mathsf{SPT}^{2}_2
statements.name: Stable polarized Ramsey theorem for pairs (2 colors)
statements.definition: For every stable coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{2} \to 2$, there are infinite sets $H_1, \dots, H_{2}$ such that $f$ is constant on all sets $\{x_1, \dots, x_{2}\} \in [\mathbb{N}]^{2}$ with $x_i \in H_i$.
statements.solution: An infinite homogeneous sequence of sets $(H_1, \dots, H_n)$.

statements.label: \mathsf{SPTT}^{2}_{<\infty}
statements.name: Stable polarized tree theorem for pairs (finitely many colors)
statements.definition: Polarized version of the tree theorem $\mathsf{TT}^{2}_{k}$: one asks for a sequence of subtrees isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$, one per coordinate; restricted to stable colorings.
statements.instance: A coloring of the 2-element chains of $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$.
statements.solution: A sequence of 2 subtrees isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$ which is homogeneous in the polarized sense.

statements.label: \mathsf{SPTT}^{2}_2
statements.name: Stable polarized tree theorem for pairs (2 colors)
statements.definition: Polarized version of the tree theorem $\mathsf{TT}^{2}_{2}$: one asks for a sequence of subtrees isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$, one per coordinate; restricted to stable colorings.
statements.instance: A coloring of the 2-element chains of $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$.
statements.solution: A sequence of 2 subtrees isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$ which is homogeneous in the polarized sense.

statements.label: \mathsf{SRAM}
statements.name: Stable Ramsey for measure
statements.definition: Measure-theoretic variant of SRT²₂ studied by Dzhafarov (2011).

statements.label: \mathsf{SRRT}^{2}_2
statements.name: Stable rainbow Ramsey theorem for pairs (2 colors)
statements.definition: Every normal 2-bounded function $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{2} \to \mathbb{N}$ (each color used at most 2 times) has an infinite rainbow set $H$, i.e. $f$ is injective on $[H]^{2}$.
statements.solution: An infinite rainbow set.

statements.label: \mathsf{SRRT}^{3}_2
statements.name: Stable rainbow Ramsey theorem for triples (2 colors)
statements.definition: Every normal 2-bounded function $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{3} \to \mathbb{N}$ (each color used at most 2 times) has an infinite rainbow set $H$, i.e. $f$ is injective on $[H]^{3}$.
statements.solution: An infinite rainbow set.

statements.label: \mathsf{SRT}^{2}_{<\infty}
statements.name: Stable Ramsey's theorem for pairs (finitely many colors)
statements.definition: Every stable coloring $f : [\mathbb{N}]^2 \to k$ has an infinite homogeneous set for every $k$. $f : [\mathbb{N}]^2 \to k$ is stable if $\lim_y f(x, y)$ exists for every $x$.
statements.solution: An infinite homogeneous set.

statements.label: \mathsf{StCADS}
statements.name: Stable CADS
statements.definition: CADS restricted to linear orders of type $\omega + \omega^*$-like stability (Hirschfeldt–Shore).

statements.label: \mathsf{StCOH}
statements.name: Stable cohesiveness
statements.definition: COH restricted to stable sequences $\vec R$ (for each $n$, $n \in R_i$ for almost all $i$ or for almost no $i$).
statements.instance: A stable sequence of sets $\vec R$.
statements.solution: An infinite $\vec R$-cohesive set.

statements.label: \mathsf{StCRT}^{2}_2
statements.name: Cohesive Ramsey theorem for stable-like colorings for pairs (2 colors)
statements.definition: Cohesive Ramsey theorem for stable-like colorings for exponent 2 and 2 colors. See the source paper for the precise formulation.

statements.label: \mathsf{STS}^{2}
statements.name: Stable thin set theorem for pairs
statements.definition: Every stable function $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{2} \to \mathbb{N}$ has an infinite thin set $H$, i.e. $f[[H]^{2}] \neq \mathbb{N}$.
statements.solution: An infinite set $H$ with $f[[H]^{2}] \neq \mathbb{N}$.

statements.label: \mathsf{STS}^{3}
statements.name: Stable thin set theorem for triples
statements.definition: Every stable function $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{3} \to \mathbb{N}$ has an infinite thin set $H$, i.e. $f[[H]^{3}] \neq \mathbb{N}$.
statements.solution: An infinite set $H$ with $f[[H]^{3}] \neq \mathbb{N}$.

statements.label: \mathsf{STT}^{2}_{<\infty}
statements.name: Stable tree theorem for pairs (finitely many colors)
statements.definition: For every stable coloring $f$ of the $2$-element chains of $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$ with k colors for every $k$, there is a subtree $S \subseteq 2^{<\mathbb{N}}$ isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$ on whose chains $f$ is constant.
statements.instance: A stable coloring of $[2^{<\mathbb{N}}]^{2}$ with k colors.
statements.solution: A homogeneous subtree isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$.

statements.label: \mathsf{STT}^{2}_2
statements.name: Stable tree theorem for pairs (2 colors)
statements.definition: For every stable coloring $f$ of the $2$-element chains of $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$ with 2 colors, there is a subtree $S \subseteq 2^{<\mathbb{N}}$ isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$ on whose chains $f$ is constant.
statements.instance: A stable coloring of $[2^{<\mathbb{N}}]^{2}$ with 2 colors.
statements.solution: A homogeneous subtree isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$.

statements.label: \mathsf{TS}^{2}
statements.name: Thin set theorem for pairs
statements.definition: Every function $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{2} \to \mathbb{N}$ has an infinite thin set $H$, i.e. $f[[H]^{2}] \neq \mathbb{N}$.
statements.solution: An infinite set $H$ with $f[[H]^{2}] \neq \mathbb{N}$.

statements.label: \mathsf{TS}^{3}
statements.name: Thin set theorem for triples
statements.definition: Every function $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{3} \to \mathbb{N}$ has an infinite thin set $H$, i.e. $f[[H]^{3}] \neq \mathbb{N}$.
statements.solution: An infinite set $H$ with $f[[H]^{3}] \neq \mathbb{N}$.

statements.label: \mathsf{TT}^1_{<\infty}
statements.name: Tree theorem for singletons
statements.definition: For every $k$, every coloring $f : 2^{<\mathbb{N}} \to k$ has a homogeneous subtree isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$.
statements.instance: A number $k$ and a coloring $f : 2^{<\mathbb{N}} \to k$.
statements.solution: A homogeneous subtree isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$.

statements.label: \mathsf{TT}^1_2
statements.name: Tree theorem for singletons (2 colors)
statements.definition: Every coloring $f : 2^{<\mathbb{N}} \to 2$ has a homogeneous subtree isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$.
statements.solution: A homogeneous subtree isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$.

statements.label: \mathsf{TT}^{2}_{<\infty}
statements.name: Tree theorem for pairs (finitely many colors)
statements.definition: For every coloring $f$ of the $2$-element chains of $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$ with k colors for every $k$, there is a subtree $S \subseteq 2^{<\mathbb{N}}$ isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$ on whose chains $f$ is constant.
statements.instance: A coloring of $[2^{<\mathbb{N}}]^{2}$ with k colors.
statements.solution: A homogeneous subtree isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$.

statements.label: \mathsf{TT}^{2}_2
statements.name: Tree theorem for pairs (2 colors)
statements.definition: For every coloring $f$ of the $2$-element chains of $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$ with 2 colors, there is a subtree $S \subseteq 2^{<\mathbb{N}}$ isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$ on whose chains $f$ is constant.
statements.solution: A homogeneous subtree isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$.

statements.label: \mathsf{TT}^{3}_2
statements.name: Tree theorem for triples (2 colors)
statements.definition: For every coloring $f$ of the $3$-element chains of $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$ with 2 colors, there is a subtree $S \subseteq 2^{<\mathbb{N}}$ isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$ on whose chains $f$ is constant.
statements.solution: A homogeneous subtree isomorphic to $2^{<\mathbb{N}}$.

statements.label: \mathsf{WSCAC}
statements.name: Weakly stable chain–antichain principle
statements.definition: CAC restricted to weakly stable partial orders (Patey, "Partial orders and immunity").

statements.label: \mathsf{WSRRT}^{2}_2
statements.name: Weakly stable rainbow Ramsey theorem for pairs (2 colors)
statements.definition: Every weakly stable 2-bounded function $f : [\mathbb{N}]^{2} \to \mathbb{N}$ (each color used at most 2 times) has an infinite rainbow set $H$, i.e. $f$ is injective on $[H]^{2}$.
statements.solution: An infinite rainbow set.

statements.label: 2\text{-}\mathsf{WWKL}
statements.name: 2-Weak weak König's lemma
statements.definition: WWKL relativized to the jump: every $\Delta^0_2$-tree of positive measure has a path.
statements.instance: A $\Delta^0_2$ binary tree of positive measure.
statements.solution: A path through it.

statements.label: \mathsf{LLPO}
statements.name: Lesser limited principle of omniscience
statements.definition: Given $p \in 2^{\mathbb{N}}$ with at most one $1$, find $i \in \{0, 1\}$ such that $p(2n + i) = 0$ for all $n$. Equivalently (Weihrauch), choice from a nonempty co-c.e. subset of $\{0, 1\}$ ($\mathsf{C}_2$).
statements.instance: A sequence $p \in 2^{\mathbb{N}}$ with at most one $1$.
statements.solution: A parity $i$ such that $p$ is zero on all positions of parity $i$.

statements.label: \mathsf{LPO}
statements.name: Limited principle of omniscience
statements.definition: Given $p \in 2^{\mathbb{N}}$, decide whether $p$ is the constant zero sequence.
statements.solution: $1$ if $p = 0^\omega$, and $0$ otherwise.

statements.label: \mathsf{C}_{\mathbb{N}}
statements.name: Closed choice on the natural numbers
statements.definition: Given an enumeration of the complement of a nonempty set $A \subseteq \mathbb{N}$, find an element of $A$. The problems Weihrauch below it are those computable with finitely many mind changes.
statements.instance: An enumeration of $\mathbb{N} \setminus A$ for some nonempty $A$.
statements.solution: An element of $A$.

statements.label: \lim
statements.name: Limit operation
statements.definition: Given a convergent sequence $(p_n)$ in $\mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}$, find its limit.
statements.instance: A convergent sequence $(p_n)_n$ in Baire space.
statements.solution: $\lim_n p_n$.

statements.label: \mathsf{IVT}
statements.name: Intermediate value theorem
statements.definition: Every continuous $f : [0, 1] \to \mathbb{R}$ with $f(0) \cdot f(1) < 0$ has a zero. Weihrauch equivalent to connected choice on $[0, 1]$.
statements.solution: A real $x \in [0,1]$ with $f(x) = 0$.

statements.label: \mathsf{BWT}_{\mathbb{R}}
statements.name: Bolzano–Weierstrass theorem
statements.definition: Every bounded sequence of real numbers has a cluster point.
statements.solution: A cluster point of the sequence.

statements.label: \mathsf{WKL}'
statements.name: Jump of weak König's lemma
statements.definition: The jump of $\mathsf{WKL}$: given a sequence converging to (a code of) an infinite binary tree, find a path through the limit tree.
statements.instance: A convergent sequence of codes for an infinite binary tree $T$.
statements.solution: An infinite path through $T$.

statements.label: \mathsf{WKL}''
statements.name: Double jump of weak König's lemma
statements.definition: The jump of $\mathsf{WKL}'$.
statements.instance: A double limit of codes for an infinite binary tree $T$.
statements.solution: An infinite path through $T$.

statements.label: \mathsf{DS}
statements.name: Descending sequences in ill-founded orders
statements.definition: Every ill-founded linear order has an infinite descending sequence.
statements.solution: An infinite descending sequence.

statements.label: \mathsf{BS}
statements.name: Bad sequences in non-wqos
statements.definition: Every quasi-order which is not a well-quasi-order has an infinite bad sequence.
statements.instance: A quasi-order which is not a wqo.
statements.solution: An infinite bad sequence.

statements.label: \mathsf{K}_{\mathbb{N}}
statements.name: Compact choice on the natural numbers
statements.definition: Given a bound $b$ and an enumeration of the complement of a nonempty set $A \subseteq \{0, \dots, b\}$, find an element of $A$. Strongly Weihrauch equivalent to the finite parallelization $\mathsf{C}_2^*$ of LLPO.
statements.instance: A bound $b$ and an enumeration of the complement of a nonempty $A \subseteq \{0, \dots, b\}$.
statements.solution: An element of $A$.

statements.label: \mathsf{C}_{\mathbb{R}}
statements.name: Closed choice on the reals
statements.definition: Given (negative information about) a nonempty closed set $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}$, find a point of $A$. Equivalent to $\mathsf{C}_{2^{\mathbb{N}}} \times \mathsf{C}_{\mathbb{N}}$.
statements.instance: An enumeration of rational open intervals whose union is the complement of a nonempty closed $A \subseteq \mathbb{R}$.
statements.solution: A point of $A$.

statements.label: \mathsf{UC}_{\mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}}
statements.name: Unique closed choice on Baire space
statements.definition: Given a closed subset of $\mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}$ with exactly one element, find that element.
statements.instance: A tree $T \subseteq \mathbb{N}^{<\mathbb{N}}$ with exactly one infinite path.
statements.solution: The infinite path of $T$.

statements.label: \mathsf{C}_{\mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}}
statements.name: Closed choice on Baire space
statements.definition: Given a nonempty closed subset of $\mathbb{N}^{\mathbb{N}}$, find an element. The single-valued problems below it are exactly the effectively Borel measurable functions; a candidate analogue of ATR in the Weihrauch lattice.
statements.solution: An infinite path through $T$.
